answer: An agent market can pay only for buyer-funded jobs with evidence checked by an independent verifier, rather than rewarding the number of seller accounts. Suppose a courier agent carries pigment across a bridge while a zephyr blows; the buyer escrows the fee, the courier commits a time-stamped route log, and a verifier chosen after delivery checks the receipt. Payments from buyer, courier, and verifier identities under common control are excluded from rewards, and disputed jobs hold the escrow. Splitting one operator into many names creates no extra eligible work.
